tab-AAA80.proposed_name: Engine torque estimate from load and RPM, variant C of four (blend weight (1-f_A)*f_B)
tab-AAA80.what_it_does: One of four load-by-RPM maps looked up back-to-back with identical inputs. The function blends the four results bilinearly using two 0..1 factors read from RAM, and stores the blended result to 0xFFFF5D58 and 0xFFFF5D5C. This map's raw value goes to 0xFFFF5E00 and enters the blend with weight (1-[FFFF90A8])*[FFFF3234].
axis_meanings: Y (0.2..2.5): engine load in g/rev. The call passes engine_load_current [FFFF63F8] in fr4.
X (800..6800): engine speed in rpm. The call passes rpm_current [FFFF6624] in fr5.
tab-AAA80.output_units: Unknown from code. The magnitude and shape suggest Nm of engine torque (hunch).
evidence: 014EFE/014F00: fr15 is loaded from 0xFFFF63F8 (engine_load_current). 014F02/014F04: fr14 is loaded from 0xFFFF6624 (rpm_current).

014F28-014F2E: descriptor 0xAAA80 is passed to table_lookup_2D at 0xBE8E4 with fr4=fr15 (load) and fr5=fr14 (rpm). The same inputs are used for the sibling tables 0xAAA64, 0xAAA9C and 0xAAAB8 at 014F0E, 014F1E and 014F34.
014F30/014F32: the result is stored to r13-12 = 0xFFFF5E00. Siblings: AAA64 goes to 0xFFFF5E08, AAA9C to 0xFFFF5E0C, AAAB8 to 0xFFFF5E04.
014F40-014F56: fr0 = 1 - f1, where f1 is fr12 from 0xFFFF90A8. Then fr8 = f1*[5E08] + (1-f1)*[5E00] (this table), stored to 0xFFFF5D50.
014F64-014F7C: f2*[5D50] + (1-f2)*[5D54], where f2 is fr13 from 0xFFFF3234, is stored to 0xFFFF5D58 and copied to 0xFFFF5D5C. This is a bilinear blend of the four maps.

Data: exactly 0 at 0.2 g/rev. Rises roughly linearly at about 145 per g/rev. Capped at 350/360 at high load. Falls at high RPM for a given load. That is consistent with net torque (indicated minus friction rising with rpm), but magnitude alone is not proof.
tab-AAA80.weakest_link: The identity 'torque' rests only on the shape and magnitude of the data. The code shows a blended load/rpm-to-quantity map but does not consume the blended result here, and the meaning of the blend factors at FFFF90A8 and FFFF3234 is not visible.
tab-AAA80.next_step: Search for readers of 0xFFFF5D5C and 0xFFFF5D58 to see whether the blended value feeds torque-request, DBW or torque-limit logic, or is compared with a torque or pedal target. Search for writers of 0xFFFF90A8 and 0xFFFF3234 to learn what selects among the four maps, and whether they ever leave the weight (1-f1)*f2 at zero.

tab-ACA78.proposed_name: Coolant-temperature-indexed decay rate for an accumulator at 0xFFFF7378, possibly a start/after-start fuel term
tab-ACA78.what_it_does: Each time the gate passes, the value looked up against coolant temperature is multiplied by a factor at 0xFFFF7388 and subtracted from a float accumulator at 0xFFFF7378, floored at 0. That accumulator, scaled by a second coolant table and added to a base value, feeds a max() and then a 2D-table multiply whose result is stored at 0xFFFF7374.
axis_meanings: X: coolant temperature in °C (fr12 = 0xFFFF6350, ect_current)
tab-ACA78.output_units: Decrement per execution in the accumulator's own units, before the 0xFFFF7388 multiplier. The table is largest when cold (0.001 at -40 °C) and smallest when hot (0.00035 at 70 °C and above).
evidence: 0308FC/030900: descriptor 0xACA78 is passed to table_lookup_1D with fr4 = fr12, and fr12 was loaded from 0xFFFF6350 (ect_current) at 030846/030848.
0308F4-0308FA: the old accumulator [r11-40] = 0xFFFF7378 is saved to the stack at @(12,r15).
030904-03090E: fneg fr0, then fmac gives acc - table*[r11-24]; [r11-24] is 0xFFFF7388.
030910-030918: float_max(result, 0.0) is written back to 0xFFFF7378, so this is a decrement-and-floor decay.
030882-030886 and 03089C-0308A2: the multiplier at 0xFFFF7388 is set to 1.0 in one state and to the ROM constant at 0xCBE18 in the other, keyed on the result of the call to 0x23E48.
0308E2-0308F2: the decay runs only when the word at 0xFFFF67EC is greater than the value looked up from table 0xACA6C (indexed by ect_gated, stored at gbr+44), and the byte at 0xFFFF7C9D is zero.
030922-030988: three parallel accumulators (0xFFFF737C, 0xFFFF7380, 0xFFFF7384) decay the same way using tables 0xACA8C, 0xACAA0 and 0xACAB4.

0309C8/030A7C-030A9A: when r13 == 0 and the byte at @(8,r15) == 0, the code takes [-40] (this accumulator), multiplies it by [-16] (table ACAF0), adds [-8], and takes the max against the parallel path.
030AA0-030AAC: that result is multiplied by table_lookup_2D(0xAD5CC, 0xFFFF6898 value, ect_gated) and stored to 0xFFFF7374.
tab-ACA78.weakest_link: The decay mechanism is observed, but the physical meaning of the 0xFFFF7374 output is not. Nothing in this listing shows where the accumulators are initialised (an after-start kick, for example) or who reads 0xFFFF7374, so calling it fuel enrichment rests only on structure.
tab-ACA78.next_step: Search for writers of 0xFFFF7378 to find the initial or reset value; a write near the start-detect routine would confirm an after-start role. Also search for readers of 0xFFFF7374 to see whether it multiplies fuel pulse width or injector base.

fn-0E794.mechanism: Saves PR, then reads SR, clears bits 4-7 with 0xFF0F and ORs in 0xF0. This sets the interrupt mask to level 15, so all maskable interrupts are blocked. The caller's original SR is not saved anywhere. The incoming argument r4 is pushed. It calls 0x40CE with no arguments and takes the returned pointer in r0. It loads the 32-bit word at [r0+8] into r5, restores the original r4 argument from the stack, and calls 0x10800(r4 = original arg, r5 = *(ret+8)). It then pops the stack slot, restores PR and tail-jumps to 0xFBA4, so whatever 0x10800 left in r0 is passed through and 0xFBA4's return value comes back to the caller. The bytes from 0xE7BC on (a series of register pushes, r7 down to r0) belong to the next routine, probably an interrupt or trap entry stub, and are not part of this function.
fn-0E794.purpose: Most likely a kernel or RTOS service wrapper. It enters a critical section with all interrupts masked and looks up a context or control-block structure (probably the current task's) via 0x40CE. It runs a service routine on the caller's argument together with a field at offset 8 of that structure, then leaves through a common exit path at 0xFBA4. That exit probably restores the interrupt level and/or runs a scheduler/dispatch check. The specific service performed is unknown.
evidence: stc sr / and 0xFF0F / or #0xF0 / ldc r0,sr sets IMASK=15, which is an explicit interrupt-disable on SH-2.
The original SR is never saved, so restoring the interrupt level must happen elsewhere, plausibly in 0xFBA4 at a fixed level. That pattern is typical of an OS service exit or dispatch path.
r0 returned by 0x40CE is used as a struct base, and the word at offset +8 is passed as the second argument to 0x10800.
The caller's r4 is preserved across the 0x40CE call and passed unchanged as the first argument to 0x10800.
The jmp to 0xFBA4 with lds.l pr in the delay slot is a tail call, so 0xFBA4 returns directly to this function's caller.
The register-push sequence at 0xE7BC looks like the prologue of an exception or interrupt handler, consistent with this region being OS/kernel code.
fn-0E794.weakest_link: The bodies of 0x40CE, 0x10800 and 0xFBA4 are not shown. Calling 0x40CE a 'current task/context' getter and 0xFBA4 an 'interrupt restore / dispatch' exit is inferred from the call pattern, not observed.

fn-067A6.mechanism: Takes an argument in r4 and saves it in a stack slot. Calls 0x0068E0 with r4 = arg; the delay-slot store means r4 is unchanged. Calls 0x006984 with r4 = arg and r5 = 2. tab-AEB48.proposed_name: Target idle speed (RPM) vs coolant temperature, mode 2 with flag r11=1 (one of 10 mode/flag variants)
tab-AEB48.what_it_does: This is a coolant-temperature-indexed base target that is high when cold (1700) and falls to 800 when warm. It is selected when state byte GBR+80 equals 2 and flag r11 equals 1. The result is stored as a target and then approached by a rate-limited ramp, which behaves like an idle-speed target.
axis_meanings: X: coolant temperature in °C (input fr12 is loaded from 0xFFFF6350, labelled ect_current). Breakpoints run -40..110.
tab-AEB48.output_units: probably rpm (800..1700); not proven by code

0510B0-0510DE: the table is chosen only when mode byte @(80,gbr)==2 (cmp/eq #2 at 0510D6) and r11==1 (0510DC). r11 is the return value of 0x22CF4 (050E62-050EBA).

0510B6-051166: there are ten sibling 1D tables (AEB20, AEB34, AEB5C, AEB70, AEB84, AEB98, AEBAC, AEBC0, AEBD4, and this one). All are indexed by the same temperature and selected by mode and flags. This is a per-mode family of the same quantity.

05116C-0511C8: the previous value @(-112,r13) = 0xFFFF8924 is compared with the new target. A step from another temperature table (AEAF8/AEAE4/AEB0C, stored at 0xFFFF8978) is added or subtracted, then clamped to the target with float_min/float_max. This is a rate-limited ramp toward the target.
0511CA-0511D0: the ramped value is copied to @(-116,r13) = 0xFFFF8920.
0511D2-0511F2: |target - current| times a constant, divided by the step, is stored to 0xFFFF8928, which looks like a time-to-target.
0511FC-051214: a deadband check of target against current sets flag @(87,gbr), which looks like 'target reached'.
Data: values fall monotonically from 1700 cold to 800 at 70 °C and above. That matches a fast-idle schedule with an 800 rpm warm idle, but a magnitude match is not an identification.
tab-AEB48.weakest_link: Nothing in this function shows that the ramped value (0xFFFF8920/0xFFFF8924) is compared against engine speed. The 'rpm' unit rests only on magnitude and shape. It could instead be another idle-related target with similar scaling, such as an airflow or idle-control-valve target.
tab-AEB48.next_step: Search for code that reads 0xFFFF8920 or 0xFFFF8924 (GBR-relative @(0,gbr)/@(4,gbr) when GBR=0xFFFF8920, or absolute literals). If a reader subtracts the engine-speed RAM variable from it, or feeds it into the idle feedback PI, the table is the target idle RPM. Also find which input 0x22CF4 returns, since that sets r11 and decides which variant (this table or AEB5C) is used.

fn-0FC04.mechanism: Stores the constant 0x0FB0, apparently a table pointer, into RAM 0xFFFF5B64. It then calls 0x00FD34. If that returns -1 it calls 0x00FD6A instead, and the result is kept at @(4,r15). If the final result is -1, or the byte at 0xFFFF415C is not 1, it simply returns. Otherwise: (1) it raises the SR interrupt mask to 15, blocking all maskable interrupts; (2) it calls 0x00FBBA(2); (3) it writes 0x77 to byte 0xFFFFBFAD, which is near the top of on-chip RAM; (4) inside critical_section_enter/exit (arg 0xE0), it reads item 20 via 0x6BC4, clears bit 3 (AND 0xF7) and writes it back via 0x6BF0(20, value); (5) it loads the pointer at 0xFFFF5B64 (0x0FB0), reads a function pointer from that address and calls it with r4=1 and r5=the low byte of the result; (6) it enters an infinite self-loop at 0x00FC72 ('bra 0x00FC72'). Code from 0x00FC7E onward belongs to a neighbouring function.
fn-0FC04.purpose: Most likely a fatal-fault or reset-request path. When a check returns a code other than -1 and a mode flag is 1, it locks out interrupts, leaves a marker (0x77) in RAM that survives reset, clears a control bit, calls a handler through a vector with the code, and then hangs, presumably so the watchdog resets the ECU.

'bra 0x00FC72' with nop is an unconditional self-loop: the function never returns on this path.
0x77 is written to 0xFFFFBFAD; mov.w sign-extends 0xBFAD, and that address is in high on-chip RAM, consistent with a reset-reason marker.

fn-3F374.mechanism:
Prologue: saves fr12-fr15 and GBR, sets GBR to 0xFFFF7E90, and reserves an 80-byte frame. Reads rpm_current (0xFFFF6624), floats at 0xFFFF62F8 and 0xFFFF65FC, ect_current (0xFFFF6350), 0xFFFF7F68 and 0xFFFF7FBC. Reads byte flags at 8F16 (mode selector r12), 8F24, 85D7, 5BE3, 65BF and 7D18, plus the byte returned by the call to 0x5EB32.

Two hold timers, GBR+113 and GBR+114 (0xFFFF7F01 and 0xFFFF7F02). Each mirrors one flag (5BE3 or 65BF), with the flag's previous value kept at GBR+115 and GBR+116. While the flag is 1 the timer is cleared. On the flag's 1-to-0 edge the timer is reloaded from calibration byte 0xD2974 or 0xD2975. Otherwise it counts down to 0.

The output is four floats: [sp+12], fr13, fr12 and fr15. They are picked by a priority chain:
(a) mode 8F16==3: all four = 7F0C + 8258*const - cal D2A34.
(b) mode 8F16==1: all four = the float at 0xFFFF7EDC.
(c) flags 8F24, 85D7 and the 0x5EB32 result all ==1, 7F68<=0 and rpm < cal D2A08: all four = 7F1C.
(d) This case needs every one of the following:
  - 62F8 < D2A0C;
  - 65FC < D2A10;
  - rpm inside the window [D2A14, D2A18);
  - timer 1 > 0;
  - flag 5BE3 == 0;
  - ECT >= D2A1C.
  If all hold, all four = cal D2A38.
(e) The same test against the second calibration set D2A20-D2A30, with timer 2 and flag 65BF: all four = cal D2A3C.
(f) Flag 7D18==1: base = 7F0C+8260+81F0, added to each element of the 4-float array at 0xFFFF81DC.
(g) Otherwise a long sum is built.
  - Additive terms (+): 7F0C, ECT-stack slot [sp+4] = 7F68, 7F6C, 7F74, 81EC, 8028, 803C, 805C, 80B4, 80C4, 80F0.
  - Subtracted terms (-): 7FBC, 8000, 8038, 8084, 80E8.
  - Calibration byte 0xD2976 decides how the terms are combined. If it equals 0x5A, all terms are summed. Otherwise the five terms 803C, 805C, 8028, 80C4, 7F6C and 80F0 are reduced with float_min, and 7FBC/8000 are combined with float_max (the larger is subtracted).
  - The result is added per element to two 4-float arrays, 0xFFFF81DC[i] and 0xFFFF8088[i].

All paths branch to a common tail (0x3F760/0x3F88E, not shown). The address of float_min is stashed at [sp+20], and the tail probably clamps and stores the results.
fn-3F374.purpose: Most likely the final per-cylinder ignition advance. It takes a base value (7F0C), adds a set of correction terms and subtracts others (likely knock/retard terms 7FBC/8000), then applies two per-cylinder 4-element offset arrays. Special modes override with fixed values: a cranking/test mode (8F16==3 or 1), and conditional fixed-timing windows. Those windows are gated by rpm range, low load, coolant temperature and post-event hold timers. The windows may be idle or post-start events, but this is not confirmed.
evidence: Four parallel outputs, each formed as scalar + 0xFFFF81DC[i] (+ 0xFFFF8088[i]) with i=0..3, indicate a per-cylinder quantity.

A base value plus many RAM terms, some explicitly subtracted, with a calibration switch (0xD2976==0x5A) choosing between summing everything and taking min/max of the terms, looks like a correction stack.
rpm_current and ect_current are verified inputs. They are used in rpm-window and coolant-minimum gates together with 62F8/65FC upper limits before a fixed calibration value (D2A38/D2A3C) is forced.
GBR+113/114 are down-counters reloaded from calibration bytes D2974/D2975 on the falling edge of flags 5BE3/65BF, i.e. hold timers after an event.
Mode byte 8F16 values 3 and 1 bypass all of this, either with a fixed RAM value (7EDC) or with 7F0C plus a scaled 8258 term minus a calibration value.
fn-3F374.weakest_link: Nothing shown verifies that the quantity is ignition timing rather than another per-cylinder value. None of the summed RAM variables (7F0C, 8000, 81DC, 8088, etc.) is cross-checked, and the store/clamp tail beyond 0x3F75E is outside the listing.

fn-7C280.mechanism: GBR=0xFFFFA158 for the whole function. It loads a 16-bit limit from 0xFFFF2BFC and keeps a 16-bit counter at 0xFFFF9FB2. (1) If the low nibbles of request bytes GBR+0, GBR+1 and GBR+2 are all zero, the counter is cleared and the output code at GBR+161 is set to 0. (2) If any request bit is set and counter > limit, the counter is cleared, bit0 of GBR+37 is cleared, and exactly one request bit is cleared. The scan order is byte0 bits0-3, then byte1 bits0-3, then byte2 bits0-1. The output code is then set to 0. (3) If counter <= limit and bit0 of GBR+37 is clear, the counter and output are cleared. (4) If counter <= limit and bit0 of GBR+37 is set, the counter is incremented through uint16_add_sat(counter,1). The highest-priority set request bit then picks a code that is written to GBR+161. The codes are: byte0 b0->1, b1->2, b2->4, b3->8; byte1 b0->5, b1->6, b2->10, b3->9; byte2 b0->3, b1->12. Finally, bits 0-3 of GBR+161 are copied one each to bit0 of flag bytes GBR+38, +39, +40 and +41, by setting or clearing that bit. The function then restores the stack and GBR and tail-jumps to 0x0003D2FC. The many stores of r0/r2 into stack slots @(4..116,r15) are compiler spill writes and are never read back.
fn-7C280.purpose: Unknown. The code is a timed sequencer. Ten pending request bits, taken in fixed priority order, each produce a 4-bit on/off pattern on four output flags. The pattern is held while an arm flag (GBR+37 bit0, set elsewhere) is on and the counter has not exceeded a limit. When the time runs out, the arm flag is dropped and the serviced request is consumed. The codes form the full set of 1-hot and 2-hot 4-bit patterns (1,2,4,8 / 5,6,10,9 / 3,12). That suggests four discrete drive lines tested singly and in pairs, for example an actuator or output self-test or a phase pattern. This reading is not established by the code shown.

(b) If the stored previous flag (0xFFFF6555, GBR+25) == 1 or the current flag == 1, the outputs are set directly with no filtering: 653C, 6540, 6544 and 6548 get B, and 654C gets A. If neither condition holds, the filter path runs. The filter path writes 653C = B and 654C = A. It then updates 6540, 6544 and 6548 with float_lag_filter(B, previous value, coefficient from 0xC3184 / 0xC3188 / 0xC318C, constant from 0x21CC0), giving three lag-filtered copies of B with separately calibrated rates. Finally it stores (flag == 1) into 0xFFFF6555 for the next call.

The result is 1 only if every one of these tests passes: (1) the float at 0xFFFF7888 is >= the calibration float at 0xCC024 (the code fails if cal > value); (2) the same float is < the calibration float at 0xCC028; (3) float_abs_diff(float @0xFFFF7890, 0.0), i.e. |x|, is < the calibration float at 0xCC02C; (4) the byte at 0xFFFF78A5 (GBR+29) equals 1; (5) if the byte at 0xFFFF78A1 (GBR+25) is non-zero, the byte at 0xFFFF789C (GBR+20) must be >= the calibration byte at 0xCBBE6, compared as signed ints after zero-extension; if that byte is zero this test is skipped; (6) the float at 0xFFFF7AB4 is <= the calibration float at 0xCC040. Any failure stores 0. Afterwards it loads r4=0x00063A5C and r5=0 (apparently setting up a following call), cleans up the stack and restores GBR/PR. The listing ends before any rts or jump, so that call is not seen.
fn-34778.purpose: Most likely an enable or 'conditions met' flag for some monitor or learning routine. The conditions are: a parameter inside a calibrated window, a second quantity (possibly a rate or deviation) near zero, a state byte equal to 1, an optional counter or timer having reached a calibrated minimum, and a further variable below a limit. Which subsystem it serves cannot be told from this code.
evidence: All results go through mov.b r0,@(28,gbr) with GBR=0xFFFF7888, i.e. the byte 0xFFFF78A4, and r0 is set only to 0 or 1
The two fcmp/gt tests against 0xCC024 and 0xCC028 bound the float at 0xFFFF7888 to a window
float_abs_diff is called with fr5=0 (fldi0) on the float at 0xFFFF7890, which gives |x|; it is compared against 0xCC02C
The byte at GBR+29 must be exactly 1; the test on GBR+20 >= the byte at 0xCBBE6 is gated by the GBR+25 byte being non-zero
The float at 0xFFFF7AB4 must not exceed the calibration value at 0xCC040
None of the addresses carries a verified name
fn-34778.weakest_link: None of the RAM variables or calibration constants is identified, and the helper at 0x029824 plus the trailing call setup (r4=0x63A5C) are not visible. The subsystem, and so any meaningful name beyond 'enable flag', is unsupported; the bitwise logic itself is observed.

fn-44DB0.mechanism: Saves PR and fr14. Reads engine_load_current (float at 0xFFFF63F8) into fr4 and also keeps a copy in fr14. It calls float_lag_filter (0x000BEA40) with fr4 = current load, fr5 = the previous filtered value from RAM 0xFFFF81F4 (0xFFFF81F8 - 4), fr6 = a ROM calibration float at 0x000D2E18 (most likely the filter coefficient) and fr7 = a float constant from the literal pool at 0x044F50. It writes the result (fr0) back to 0xFFFF81F4, so that variable is a lag-filtered copy of engine load. It then computes current load minus the filtered load and stores that difference as a float at 0xFFFF81F8, then returns. Code after the rts/nop at 0x044DDE belongs to neighbouring functions and is not part of this one: at 0x044DE0 there is a 16-bit counter at 0xFFFF8224 that is cleared when the byte at 0xFFFF81BA is nonzero and otherwise counts up, saturating at 0xFFFF; another function's prologue starts at 0x044E04.
fn-44DB0.purpose: Keeps a smoothed (first-order lagged) engine load and a load-minus-filtered-load signal. That difference acts as a high-pass, rate-of-change measure of load. It is most likely used to detect load transients such as tip-in/tip-out or load-change enrichment and compensation logic, but no consumer of 0xFFFF81F8 is shown.

fr6 comes from the ROM calibration address 0x000D2E18 and fr7 from a pool constant, consistent with a coefficient and a scale or limit argument
fsub fr8,fr14 followed by fmov.s fr14,@r6 stores load - filtered load at 0xFFFF81F8

fn-44DB0.weakest_link: The exact argument semantics of float_lag_filter (which of fr6/fr7 is the coefficient) and the values at 0x000D2E18 and 0x044F50 are not shown. The downstream use of the delta at 0xFFFF81F8 is not visible, so the 'transient detection' purpose is not confirmed.

fn-45A84.mechanism: GBR is set to 0xFFFF8258, the base of a RAM block. The function reads byte 0xFFFF3244 and masks bit 0, then reads byte 0xFFFF8233. It writes 0 to byte 0xFFFF8278 (GBR+32) if any of these hold: byte 0xFFFF8233 is non-zero; bit 0 of 0xFFFF3244 is set; byte 0xFFFF8277 (GBR+31, zero-extended) is not 1; or the ROM float at 0x000D2EDC is greater than the RAM float at 0xFFFF8258 (fcmp/gt fr8,fr9 with fr9 = calibration and fr8 = RAM value). Otherwise it writes 1. Put another way, the flag is 1 only when 8233 == 0, bit 0 of 3244 is clear, 8277 == 1 and float[8258] >= cal[0xD2EDC]. The byte of 8277 is also spilled to the stack and never used. GBR is saved and restored around the function. Everything after rts/ldc.l at 0x045AC2 is the literal pool, not code.
fn-45A84.purpose: unknown. Structurally this is an enable/condition flag: a module state byte (8277) must be 1, two inhibit conditions (8233 non-zero, bit 0 of 3244) must be absent, and a float quantity at the head of the same RAM block must have reached a calibrated minimum. Which subsystem it belongs to cannot be told from this code.
evidence: mov.l @(0x045B38) loads 0xFFFF8258 into GBR; mov.b @(31,gbr) therefore reads 0xFFFF8277 and mov.b r0,@(32,gbr) writes 0xFFFF8278
Pool word at 0x045AD8 is 0xFFFF3244; it is read as a byte and ANDed with 1, and a non-zero result makes the output 0
Byte at 0xFFFF8233 is tested with tst; a non-zero value makes the output 0
cmp/eq #1 on 8277: any value other than 1 makes the output 0
fr9 = float at ROM 0x000D2EDC, fr8 = float at RAM 0xFFFF8258; when fcmp/gt sets T (cal > RAM) the output is 0, otherwise 1
Only one store: a 0/1 byte to 0xFFFF8278
fn-45A84.weakest_link: None of the RAM addresses (3244, 8233, 8258, 8277, 8278) or the calibration at 0xD2EDC is named or cross-referenced, so the subsystem and physical meaning of the threshold comparison are unknown.

It is multiplied with two rpm-indexed 2D tables and an ECT table, and the product is clamped to 0..80 to form a ceiling for a quantity this routine computes and rate-limits. What that quantity is cannot be fixed from this listing.

fn-0F320.mechanism: Saves PR. Loads the sign-extended word 0xF6E8, which gives the address 0xFFFFF6E8 in the SH7058 on-chip peripheral register space, not RAM. It does a 16-bit read of that register into r3. The value is thrown away, because r3 is immediately overwritten with the call target. It then writes the 16-bit constant 0x000B (11) back to the same register; that store sits in the delay slot of the first call. It calls 0x00007110, then calls 0x00007D26, then restores PR and tail-jumps to 0x0000BB6C, so the third routine returns straight to this function's caller. Everything after 0x00F33A is literal pool or neighbouring data (a word table 0x00A0..0x00B0, bit-clear masks 0xFF7F/0xFEFF/..., and the call-target literals) and is not executed by this function.
fn-0F320.purpose: Probably the body of an interrupt or periodic handler. It acknowledges or clears a hardware status/flag register (a dummy read followed by a write, the usual SH7058 sequence for clearing flags), or rewrites a control register, and then runs three sub-tasks in a fixed order. What the tasks are and which peripheral the register belongs to cannot be told from this listing.
evidence: mov.w @(0x00F35E),r4 loads 0xF6E8; the word load sign-extends it to 0xFFFFF6E8, which is in the on-chip I/O area (above the RAM at 0xFFFF0000-0xFFFFBFFF), probably in the ATU-II timer block
mov.w @r4,r3 reads the register, and r3 is overwritten by the next mov.l before anyone uses it: a dummy read
mov #11,r2 / mov.w r2,@r4 in the jsr delay slot writes 0x000B to that register
jsr 0x7110, then jsr 0x7D26, then jmp 0xBB6C with lds.l @r15+,pr in the delay slot: two calls and a tail call
The function takes no arguments and returns no value of its own
fn-0F320.weakest_link: Which peripheral register lives at 0xFFFFF6E8, and whether writing 0x000B clears flags or sets a control mode, is not confirmed; there is no register map here. The roles of 0x7110, 0x7D26 and 0xBB6C are unknown, and so is whether this routine is reached from an interrupt vector.

tab-AF2B8.proposed_name: Gear- and RPM-dependent upper limit, probably a torque ceiling (base mode, operand of the min chain)
tab-AF2B8.what_it_does: In the default mode, where the function argument r4/r14 is 0, this descriptor is loaded into gbr+224 and looked up against two inputs that likely carry RPM (Y axis) and gear (X axis). The result is stored to 0xFFFF8714 and then min'ed against a sibling table's result, so it acts as a ceiling. That ceiling feeds a weighted blend whose result goes to stack slot 68. The data allows 500 in gears 1–3 and 350 in gears 4–6, flat across RPM.
axis_meanings: Y (800..6800): almost certainly engine speed in rpm. It is the float from RAM 0xFFFF679C, copied to stack slot 36 at 0BCEF8–0BCEFE and passed as one lookup argument.

0BD118 branches to 0BD228, so the gbr+224 lookup runs on both branches of the 0BD0D2 test.

tab-AE62C.proposed_name: Per-cylinder ignition timing compensation, 4th of a set of four (likely cylinder 4), RPM x load

axis_meanings: Y (1200..6400): engine speed, rpm. The value passed in fr4 comes from 0xFFFF6624 rpm_current.
X (0.5..2.3): engine load, g/rev. The value passed in fr5 comes from 0xFFFF63F8 engine_load_current.
tab-AE62C.output_units: probably degrees of ignition advance (uint8 x 0.3515625 - 45, so raw 128 = 0; 0.3516 deg per count); unconfirmed
evidence: 0x044190/0x044192: fr15 is loaded from 0xFFFF6624 (rpm_current). At 0x0441F2 it is passed as fr4, the first axis input.
0x044194/0x044196: fr12 is loaded from 0xFFFF63F8 (engine_load_current). At 0x0441F8 it is passed as fr5. The axis breakpoints 1200..6400 and 0.5..2.3 match rpm and g/rev.

Cell scaling 90/256 per count with a -45 offset is a typical Subaru ignition-angle encoding. The data are sparse small positive steps (1 to 3 counts) in scattered cells, which looks like a per-cylinder trim rather than a base map.

A pin toggled like this is typically a heartbeat or external-watchdog kick, but what the pin drives cannot be determined from this code.
